request.prompt:
A Python function fails its tests.

Code:
```python
def even_odd_count(num):
    even_count = 0
    odd_count = 0
    for i in str(abs(num)):
        if int(i)%2==0:
            even_count +=1
    return (even_count, odd_count)
```

Test output:
```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "solution.py", line 36, in <module>
    check(even_odd_count)
    ~~~~~^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "solution.py", line 23, in check
    assert even_odd_count(7) == (0, 1)
           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
AssertionError
```

In at most three sentences, state the root cause of the bug. Do not write code.

response.text: The function never updates `odd_count`, so it always returns `(even_count, 0)` regardless of odd digits. This causes the assertion for `even_odd_count(7)` to fail because it expects `(0, 1)`.
